build.note: Read from saved raw captures; no export, no new capture.

question: L99 predicted from stored capsules on the rest pose that the centre line from 108 to 136 cm takes limb damage (22 with the M433) where the site shows chest (26). What does the game do?

sourceFacts.method: Operator video 'Battlefield 6 2026.10.10 - 15.28.41.03.mp4' (SHA-256 f4eca5b6e610d3c4ea0326cad4a19aae1b31a1a4ce4e45249201567516ce0c75, 2560 x 1440, 139.8 s): a custom range with enemy bot soldiers at 5 m, M433, single shots aiming down sights, damage numbers shown. Each hit was located by the change of the on-screen hit counter (56 hits); for each, the frame 10 frames earlier (aim point) and 4 frames later (damage number) were cropped side by side (body.py, body00-06.jpg). Aim points were judged by eye by the parent.

control.description: Headshots show 36 = 26 x 1.4, and thigh hits 22 = 26 x 0.84, the site's M433 values inside 21 m.

head.note: 36 = 26 x 1.4. In hits 27, 28, 29, 34, 35, 40, 41 and 42 the sight dot is above or beside the visible helmet in the frame about 0.15 s before the hit registers, and the hit counts as a headshot.

sourceFacts.boundary: Hits 9 (26) and 10 (22) on the same bot are a few centimetres apart at upper-belly height; hits 6 (26) and 7, 8 (22) agree.

inference: Mid-chest and upper-chest hits do full damage (26). The site's chest zone is right; the L99 rest-pose capsule projection, which put limb damage there, is not what the game does for a soldier in the aiming stance.
The change from 26 to 22 lies at about upper-belly height, which is where the site draws its chest and stomach boundary.
Hits beside and just above the visible helmet count as headshots in several cases, which agrees with the stored head capsule being larger than the site's head artwork. The size was not measured.

The stored capsules are probably used, but on the animated pose: in the aiming stance the torso leans forward, which brings the large chest sphere in front of the abdomen capsule. This explanation is not tested.
unresolved: Aim heights were judged by eye from the sight picture and are not in centimetres. The aim frame is about 0.17 s before the hit registers and the bots move slightly.
Targets were bots facing the shooter in an aiming stance; an upright idle soldier and the back view were not tested.
Head size beyond the helmet is observed, not measured.
siteImpact: None. No Analyzer data, simulation or UI change.

leads.title: Operator video (M433, bots at 5 m): mid-chest hits do 26, belly and limbs 22, head 36; the capsule rest-pose prediction of 22 at mid-chest is not supported
leads.summary: Operator video, M433 at 5 m against bot soldiers, 56 hits: mid-chest and upper-chest hits do 26, belly, arm and leg hits 22, headshots 36. The 26-to-22 change is at upper-belly height, as the site draws it. The L99 capsule prediction for the chest aim point is not supported; no site change. Headshots register slightly outside the visible helmet. 2 raw-offset checks matched.
leads.reopenWhen: A measured test (known heights, upright target or back view) is wanted for the head size or the exact boundary height.
leads.statusNote: L99 chest prediction not supported in game; site chest zone kept.

assets.conclusion: Head capsule length 0.06 and radius 0.14 re-read; the stored capsules exist, but their rest-pose projection does not predict the in-game chest zone.
